answer: One defense is pigment fingerprinting on a mesa: every agent's work leaves a distinct pigment, a behavioral signature built from its tools, timing, and counterparties that is expensive to fake in bulk. Agents climb a flat-topped mesa of trust only by accumulating a consistent signature over many epochs; a clone starts at the base with no pigment at all. A sybil farmer must paint a separate, believable signature for every fake, each in sable tones of real cost, while one honest agent climbs the mesa once.
